guide.summary: Calendly supports OAuth 2.0 for third-party apps, and Composio provides a managed OAuth app, so you can prototype without registering anything. Registering your own app is a short self-serve form in a separate developer account. The docs describe no review process, but I could not confirm that none exists, so check the developer console before promising a go-live date.

composio.note: Composio lists Calendly under Composio-managed OAuth. Scopes are fixed by the OAuth app/auth config, not chosen by end users. Changing scopes means reconnecting accounts.

need_own_app.answer: Not to start. Composio's managed OAuth app works for prototyping. Create your own app when you need your own branding, a specific scope set, or your own quota and credentials.
reasons: You want your own app name and consent screen shown to users
You need control over the exact scope set, since users cannot pick scopes individually
You want your own client ID/secret and rate-limit isolation
You want separate Sandbox and Production apps

scenarios.label: Prototype with Composio managed auth
scenarios.when_this_applies: Internal testing or early development where Composio's app name and default scopes are acceptable.

hands_on.basis: No setup is needed on the Calendly side per c1, but I have no measured time. Estimate from step count: likely minutes.

waiting.basis: c1: you do not need to register an OAuth app.

scenarios.label: Own Sandbox OAuth app for development
scenarios.when_this_applies: You want your own client ID/secret but are still developing, using a localhost redirect.

hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count, not measured. Registration is one form (c3, c4).

waiting.basis: Docs describe no approval for Sandbox apps, but this is not confirmed.

scenarios.label: Own Production OAuth app with live customer data
scenarios.when_this_applies: You go live with your own branding, scopes, and credentials. Requires an HTTPS redirect URI.

hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count, not measured. Includes a second app, one-time secret capture, and the Composio auth config.

waiting.basis: Calendly docs read describe no review or verification for Production apps. I found no evidence either way, and no timeline reports.

scenarios.approval: No review documented. Not confirmed. Verify in the developer console.

prerequisites.title: Calendly developer account
prerequisites.detail: Sign up with GitHub or Google. This is separate from your normal Calendly user account.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS redirect URI (Production)
prerequisites.detail: Use the callback URL shown in your Composio dashboard for the auth config. Production requires HTTPS. Do not hard-code a URL from elsewhere.

prerequisites.title: Scope decision
prerequisites.detail: Pick the scopes your app needs. The scope list page was not read, so scope names are unconfirmed here. Read https://developer.calendly.com/docs/authentication/scopes.

prerequisites.title: Composio account and API key
prerequisites.detail: Needed to create the auth config.

steps.title: Decide whether managed auth is enough
steps.detail: If Composio's app name and default scopes are acceptable, use managed auth and skip the rest. Otherwise continue.
steps.done_when: You have chosen managed or custom auth.

steps.title: Draft the scope list
steps.detail: An agent can read the Calendly scopes page and the Composio tools you plan to use, then propose the minimum scope set.
inputs: List of Composio Calendly tools you will call
steps.done_when: You have a reviewed scope list.

steps.title: Create a Calendly developer account
steps.detail: Sign up with GitHub or Google.
steps.done_when: You can see the developer console.

steps.title: Get the Composio callback URI
steps.detail: In the Composio dashboard, start creating a Calendly auth config with custom credentials and copy the redirect/callback URI it shows.

steps.title: Create the OAuth app
steps.detail: Enter name and kind (web or native), pick the environment, paste the Composio callback URI, and select scopes. Use Sandbox first. Create a second app for Production, which needs an HTTPS redirect.
steps.done_when: The app is created and the credentials page is shown.

steps.title: Copy the client ID, client secret, and webhook signing key
steps.detail: The secret and signing key are shown only at creation. Store them in a secrets manager now.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Paste the client ID and secret into the Calendly auth config in Composio and use the same scopes. Then connect a test account.
steps.done_when: A test account connects and a tool call succeeds.

steps.title: Check whether Production needs approval
steps.detail: Docs describe no review. Check the developer console and ask developer support if unsure.
steps.done_when: You know whether any approval is pending.

traps.title: Client secret cannot be recovered
traps.detail: Editing the app does not reveal the secret or webhook signing key. If lost, you will likely need to create a new app or find a reset option in the console, which I did not confirm.

traps.title: Sandbox and Production are separate apps
traps.detail: Docs recommend a second app for Production, so credentials and redirect URIs differ.

traps.title: Scope changes require reconnecting
traps.detail: Users cannot pick scopes, and changing scopes means reconnecting accounts.

traps.title: Single-use refresh tokens
traps.detail: Calendly has a guide on single-use refresh tokens. I did not read it, so check how rotation interacts with your setup.

blockers.what_it_means: Production apps require HTTPS. Only Sandbox allows http://localhost.
blockers.what_to_do: Use the HTTPS callback URI from Composio, or use a Sandbox app for local tests.
blockers.agent_can_help: An agent can check that the URI is HTTPS and matches the Composio dashboard value exactly.

blockers.what_it_means: The secret is shown only once at creation.
blockers.what_to_do: Check the console for a regenerate option, otherwise create a new app and update the Composio auth config.

blockers.symptom: Authorize URL with a bad client_id lands on a login page instead of an error
blockers.what_it_means: The probe showed redirects to the Calendly login page with no obvious error. This does not tell you whether an app is registered.
blockers.what_to_do: Test the authorize URL in a browser with your real client ID after logging in.

open_questions: Does Calendly review or verify Production OAuth apps? Docs read do not say. Check the developer console or ask developer support.
Are there user caps for apps in Sandbox or unreviewed Production? Unknown.
Do end users need a paid Calendly plan to authorize an OAuth app? Unknown.
What are the scope names and rate limits? Pages exist but were not read.
How do single-use refresh tokens interact with Composio's token storage? Guide not read.

claims.text: Composio can provide the OAuth app for managed toolkits, so you do not need to register your own.
claims.quote: You do not need to register an OAuth app or supply its client ID and client secret.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Calendly end users cannot approve individual scopes. The scopes in your OAuth app are the ones requested, and changing them requires reconnecting.
claims.quote: To change Calendly permissions, update the scopes in your OAuth app/auth config and reconnect the account so a new token is issued with the updated scopes.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Registering requires a separate Calendly developer account, not your normal user account.
claims.quote: Sign up for a Calendly developer account using your Github or Google account by clicking the Sign Up button found in the top right corner of this page.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Calendly recommends Sandbox for development and a second application for Production. Sandbox allows an http localhost redirect and Production must be HTTPS.
claims.quote: For the Production environment, this must be HTTPS
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Scopes are selected when creating the OAuth app, based on the data and functionality needed.
claims.quote: Select scopes based on the Calendly data and functionality that your OAuth app requires access to.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: The client secret and webhook signing key are shown only at creation and cannot be accessed again.
claims.quote: Be sure to copy these values as you will not be able to access the Client Secret or Webhook signing key again
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: All apps should use a specific redirect_uri and PKCE with S256, though PKCE is not enforced for web apps.
claims.quote: While we will not enforce PKCE for web applications, we recommend using PKCE conforming to the RFC 7636 specification for both web and native applications.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: No review, verification, or approval process for Calendly OAuth apps was found in the docs read, and its absence is not confirmed.
claims.label: unknown

claims.text: Calendly has a separate guide on single-use refresh tokens (refresh token rotation). It was listed in the docs index but not read.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: An authorize request with an invalid client_id redirected (301, then 302) to the Calendly login page rather than returning an obvious error.
claims.label: probed

probes.purpose: Observe Calendly authorize endpoint response to an invalid client_id
Observe the authorize page response for an invalid client_id
probes.observation: Redirects to https://calendly.com/app/login. Body starts: "You are being redirected ."
